sentences.text: Shri Abhishek Singh, learned Public Prosecutor for the  respondent/State.
Shri Rajmani Singroul, learned counsel for the complainant .
Heard on I.A. No.19038/2024, 4th application under Section 430 of BNSS/389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant-Devideen Ahirwar, S/o Rajju Ahirwar.
Earlier applications, except for one which was dismissed on merit on 19/11/2020, were withdrawn.

This appeal is filed being aggrieved of judgment dated 31st October, 2018 passed in Special Case (SC POSCO) No.11/2017 by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, Panna whereby appellant has been convicted in the following manners:-
 Conviction Sentence  
 Section Act Imprisonment Fine  
 
 376(2)(i)) I.P.C. R.I. for life Rs.2,000/-
 
 
 5(d)/6 POCSO R.I. for life Rs.2,000/-
Shri Alok Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellant, submits that 2 CRA-9290-2018 Coordinate Bench while deciding the application on 19/11/2020 did not appreciate two material facts.

Firstly,
the DNA report, as discussed by learned trial Court in para-21 of its judgment, clearly make a mention of the fact that 'Y' chromosomal profile recovered from the undergarments of the victim Devideen Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199325646/
1 was containing multiple male-profile and that did not match with the 'Y' chromosomal profile obtained from the blood sample of the present appellant.

sentences.text: It is submitted that though the Coordinate Bench has placed reliance on the evidence of Dr. Bhawna Tripathi (PW-7) who has deposed that the hymen of the victim was ruptured in a multidimensional manner and there was swelling on her private parts indicating violation of her privacy, but, under same time, learned trial Court in para-35 has said that the victim had left her undergarments in the field, however, it is contrary to Ex.P/12 in which it is mentioned that two vaginal slides and samples of underwear (Paijama) were prepared, preserved and sealed.
White coloured stains present over black coloured underwear handed over to the Police Constable.

Therefore, reasonings of learned trial Court in para-35 of the impugned judgment that since undergarment of the prosecutrix was left in the open field and that has been proved by the mother of prosecutrix P.W.-4, is contrary to the statement of Dr. Bhawna Tripathi (PW-7).
Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that certain facts are required to be put into a straitjacket manner.
Firstly, there is no doubt that victim was subjected to violation of her privacy as has been deposed by the victim and Dr. Bhawna Tripathi (PW-7).

However, presence of multiple 3 CRA-9290-2018 source 'Y' chromosome has ejected from the strains available on the undergarment of the victim and they were matching with the blood sample of the present appellant, is an important circumstance which could not have been overlooked.

As far as reasoning of the learned trial Court that mother of the victim i.e. P.W.-4 had stated in her Court deposition that the clothes which the victim was wearing, were lying in the field and the statement of the prosecutrix that she was not wearing any underwear but was wearing a Kurti and a black Paijama and Dr. Bhawna Tripathi (PW-7) had seized only black underwear and had not seized Paijama/Kurti and had found white colour spots on the underwear which was presented for the DNA examination, are circumstances with which Dr. Bhawna Tripathi (PW-7) should have been confronted.

But, on careful examination of the cross-examination of Dr. Bhawna Tripathi (PW-7),
reveals that none of these suggestions have been given to her in view of the evidence of P.W.4 that the clothes were recovered from the field and also in view of the statement of the prosecutrix that she was not wearing underwear at the time of incident.
Thus, it is submitted that learned trial Court glossed over important and vital piece of evidence while recording a finding of conviction.
It is settled principle of law that if benefit of doubt is due, then it should be extended in favour of the accused.

Hence, prayer is made to suspend the sentence of the appellant and grant him bail Shri Abhishek Singh, learned Public Prosecutor and Shri Rajmani 4 CRA-9290-2018 Singroul, learned counsel for the complainant, oppose the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

Taking these facts into consideration and without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant and release him on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.19038/2024 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two sureties in the like amount Devideen Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199325646/
2 to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 02/04/2025 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
Certified copy as per rules.
